topic: A Systematic Review of Key Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems: Progress, Gaps, and Future Directions
topic_definition: Stage 2 canonical eligibility, source-faithful to the original paper's screening criteria. Eligible works are relevant to Retrieval-Augmented Generation or closely related baselines, clearly integrate retrieval with a generative language model or use retrieval to supply context to a generator, and center on knowledge-intensive tasks.
summary: Stage 2 canonical criteria restated from criteria_mds/2507.18910.md; publication-time filtering is handled by cutoff_jsons/2507.18910.json.

summary_topics.description: A Systematic Review of Key Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems: Progress, Gaps, and Future Directions

required.criterion: Paper is relevant to RAG or closely related baselines, clearly integrates a retriever with a generative language model, or uses retrieval to supply context to a generator.
Paper centers on knowledge-intensive tasks, such as open-domain question answering, fact-checking, knowledge-grounded dialogue, or other tasks benefiting from external document retrieval.
Source is peer-reviewed or otherwise reputable, including substantive preprints, technical reports, industry white papers, major AI/NLP venues, or recognized industrial R&D labs.

exclusion_criteria.criterion: Works focused strictly on retrieval or strictly on generation without explicit retrieval-augmented integration are excluded.
Works with only minimal or superficial RAG discussion and no substantial results or analyses are excluded.
Non-substantive publications, very short abstracts, publicity notes, and materials without verifiable methodology are excluded.
